item.title: Noise-resilient training of machine learning interatomic potentials
item.description:
📚 The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue
The accuracy of machine learning interatomic potentials suffers from reference data that contain numerical noise. Often originating from unconverged or inconsistent electronic-structure calculations, this noise is challenging to identify. Existing mitigation strategies, such as manual filtering or iterative refinement of outliers, require either substantial expert effort or multiple expensive retraining cycles, making them difficult to scale to large datasets. Here, we introduce a noise-resilient training method that automatically down-weighs noisy samples, without requiring additional reference calculations. Industrial robotic systems rely on predictive maintenance to prevent failures and optimize operational efficiency. However, accurately detecting faults such as protective stop and grip loss remains challenging due to high-dimensional sensor data and inherent noise. To address this, we propose a quantum multi-output network combined with cycle-consistent autoencoders, leveraging quantum feature encoding to enhance fault detection. The model effectively reduces dimensionality while mitigating quantum noise propagation, ensuring computational efficiency with fewer qubits. item.description:

This paper studies how much Quantum Processing Unit (QPU) work can be avoided while preserving optimization quality in the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA). item.title: Lateral photovoltaic effect in SiO2/TeO2/Bi2Te3/n-Si structure
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 I. A. Bondarev, M. V. Rautskii, A. S. Tarasov, T. A. Pisarenko, A. A. Yakovlev, V. V. Mararov 等7位作者
The lateral photovoltaic effect (LPE) in a SiO2/TeO2/Bi2Te3/n-Si hybrid heterostructure was investigated as a function of light wavelength, temperature, illumination position, and magnetic field. The Schottky barrier height of the structure was estimated to be ΦB = 0.3 eV using the thermionic emission model. A pronounced change in the LPE is observed near λ = 1 µm, including a reversal of the photovoltage polarity. This indicates the transition between two dominant photovoltaic channels associated with carrier photogeneration in the Si substrate and Bi2Te3 film. The Si-related contribution was found to be sensitive to the magnetic field, whereas the Bi2Te3-related contribution remains nearly unaffected. Magnetic fields are invisible yet essential components in technologies ranging from MRI scanners and particle accelerators to atomic clocks and future quantum computers. Each of these applications requires magnetic fields with specific shapes and properties. Today, creating such tailored magnetic fields requires researchers and engineers to design specialized, carefully optimized magnets or large systems of coils for each individual application—a complex and resource-intensive process.

item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Chunli Huang, Mainak Das, Nemin Wei
Spatial textures of magnetic order, such as domain walls and skyrmions, are fundamental objects in magnetism. In rhombohedral multilayer graphene, magnetic order involves spin and valley degrees of freedom, opening the possibility of qualitatively new spatial textures. Here, we explore this possibility through a microscopic study of a one-dimensional domain wall in the valley-imbalanced quarter-metal phase of rhombohedral graphene. We uncover two different classes of domain walls. One resembles a conventional magnetic domain wall, locally rotating between the two bulk states, whereas the other is intrinsically multicomponent and explores states that are not occupied in either bulk domain. Quantum supervised learning (QSL) is increasingly investigated for intrusion detection, yet its behavior under adversarial manipulation remains insufficiently characterized in network-security settings. This study presents a controlled white-box evaluation of a four-qubit variational QSL intrusion detector and a matched classical multilayer perceptron (MLP) on the UNSW-NB15 benchmark. Categorical encoding, standardization, principal component analysis to four dimensions, and scaling to [0, π] were applied consistently. A clean QSL model and a PGD-aware QSL model using 50% clean, 25% FGSM, and 25% PGD samples were evaluated against FGSM and seven-step PGD attacks at ε = 0.02π, 0.05π, and 0.10π over ten matched random seeds. item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Jeong Youn-Chang, Kim Seok, Hong Changho, Ji Se-Wan
Quantum digital signature (QDS) provides information-theoretic security and enables fundamental cryptographic functionalities, including integrity, non-repudiation, and data origin authentication. Existing QDS implementations, however, assign fixed user roles - signer, authenticator, and verifier - which limits their applicability in practical quantum networks, where role flexibility is essential. In this work, we implement a QDS protocol on a three-user fiber-optic quantum network in which any participant can dynamically assume the role of signer. Quantum-network capacity planning couples memory physics, finite storage, topology, and traffic. We study these interactions using a discrete-event simulator with six representative memory profiles. A household service robot has to watch for objects on the floor while it moves, and on a small, battery-powered computer the object detector is often the most expensive part of that job. Adaptive perception, which runs the detector only when and where it seems necessary, is a popular way of reducing this cost, but it is rarely evaluated in a closed loop where a missed detection can leave a task unfinished or cause a collision. We tested it in 25 photorealistic home scans that were held out from all training, with obstacles that reach the planner only through the detector.
